title: The Silent Wolf
premise: In the city of Vhalder, magic is a death sentence, and Rafael Marchetti has survived ten years by selling charms too small to notice and never speaking to beasts where anyone can see. When a feral child named Wren arrives at his door speaking the First Tongue—the language that once commanded the old gods' beasts—Rafael learns she carries an inheritance meant for him: the wolf-bond of his slaughtered family line, and with it the memory of the war the kingdoms swore never to repeat. Hunted by the Inquisitor Sera Vance, who suspects the child's gift but not his own, Rafael must choose between destroying the bond to stay invisible or awakening it to save Wren from those who would use her as a weapon. In the end, he accepts the inheritance, breaks the wolf-bond's war-magic apart rather than wield it, and flees the city with Wren—not free, but no longer hiding—leaving Vhalder's law intact but its silence permanently cracked.
about_author: Rosalind Ishikawa is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing extinct languages before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who survive by staying small, and lives quietly with an opinionated dog.

chapters.title: Charms and Cinders
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A day in his carefully small life: haggling charms in Vhalder's night market, dodging a patrol, and a brief, guilty conversation with a stray dog in the alleys. The beat is the suffocating comfort of a life built on invisibility—and the first hairline crack in it.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A mud-streaked girl appears at his shop at closing, speaking words he understands without wanting to: the First Tongue. She carries a wolf-tooth pendant he recognizes from a family he buried a decade ago. The beat is terror disguised as hospitality.

chapters.title: What the Tooth Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, fragmented and sensory. She recounts fleeing her village, guided by a voice in the tooth that called her to Rafael by name. The beat is a child's trust colliding with an adult's dread; Rafael realizes the bond chose him, not her.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sera Vance's POV. She reviews a decade of petty magic convictions and notices a pattern: charms sold near Rafael's shop, always small, always deniable. She requests his file. The beat is cold, patient menace—she is good at her job, and believes in it.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with flashbacks to the night his family's wolf-bond was exposed and burned out of them. He explains to Wren why he never answered the tooth: the last man who carried it started a war. The beat is grief weaponized into caution.

chapters.title: The Old Market Bargain
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He seeks out Odile, a smuggler who moves people, not goods, to buy Wren passage out of Vhalder. She agrees—for a price he can't pay yet, and a warning: the Inquisitor already bought passage lists. The beat is the cost of every escape rising.

chapters.title: Beasts Do Not Lie
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Left alone in the shop, she speaks to the rats in the walls and learns someone has been listening to them for weeks—a watcher paid by a man with a ledger. The beat is the child's gift revealing what Rafael's caution cannot: they are already hunted.

chapters.title: A Question of Jurisdiction
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She interrogates Rafael under pretense of a licensing inquiry and lets slip that she knows a child is in the city. Rafael lies well enough to live, badly enough to confirm her suspicion. The beat is two careful people circling, each aware of the other's teeth.

chapters.title: The Bond Beneath the Skin
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The tooth begins answering Wren through Rafael whether he consents or not—his senses sharpening, old war-instincts surfacing. He tries to bury it in the river; it returns. The beat is the horror of an inheritance that cannot be refused, only accepted or suffered.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Odile names her price: the location of the last free beast-herd, which only the wolf-bond can find. Rafael refuses and loses his only exit. Wren, having overheard, quietly offers to ask the beasts herself. The beat is the child outgrowing her protector's rules.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Dogs
chapters.summary: Alternating Rafael and Sera POV. Sera raids the night market with a warrant for 'an unregistered minor'; Rafael and Wren escape through the sewers guided by rats Wren speaks to. The beat is flight, adrenaline, and the first time Rafael uses the bond deliberately to survive.

chapters.title: What the Kingdoms Buried
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, in hiding with Odile's people. An old smuggler who fought in the Beast Wars explains the truth: the bond isn't a weapon, it's a treaty—the old gods' terms for peace, held in trust by bloodlines like his. The beat is the reframing of his curse as a responsibility.

chapters.title: The Herd at Greyfell
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The journey north to the beast-herd, Wren translating the land itself—roads that remember, crows that warn. Rafael follows, half-converted. The beat is wonder threading through danger, and Wren's growing certainty that the tooth chose them both.

chapters.title: Terms of the Treaty
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At Greyfell, the herd's ancient matriarch speaks to Rafael directly: accept the bond fully, or the treaty dies and the beasts' long patience ends. She shows him the war as the beasts remember it. The beat is awe curdling into the weight of a choice no one should carry alone.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Ascendant
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Her superiors, spooked by rumors of a living wolf-bond, grant her extraordinary powers—and a rival faction whispers about weaponizing the child instead of burning her. Sera realizes the institution she serves is worse than the magic she hunts. The beat is a true believer's first doubt.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Greyfell
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Sera's trackers find them; a member of Odile's crew sold the location. In the fight, Rafael accepts the bond to save Wren, and the power that floods him terrifies him more than the soldiers do. The beat is the price of survival paid in full: he is now exactly what the kingdom fears.

chapters.title: Wolf and Wolf-Hunter
chapters.summary: Alternating Rafael and Sera POV. Cornered, Sera orders the capture of the child, not the man—and Rafael sees she intends to protect Wren from her own faction. An uneasy, armed truce. The beat is the discovery that his enemy's conscience is his strangest ally.

chapters.title: The War That Wants Waking
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The tooth, now awake, shows Wren the full inheritance—and the war-magic coiled inside it, which the old gods designed to be unleashed by a child's voice. She understands why her village burned. The beat is a child carrying an adult's apocalypse.

chapters.title: The Choice of Marchetti
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Vhalder's faction arrives to take Wren; Sera stands with Rafael against her own order. Rafael holds the war-magic in his hands and realizes the treaty's final term: the bond-bearer may unmake the magic rather than wield it—at the cost of the bond, the beasts' protection, and his own safety forever. The beat is the climax of the inheritance theme: he chooses to end it, not own it.

chapters.title: Unmaking
chapters.summary: Rafael and Wren POV, braided. In the ruins beneath Vhalder, Rafael breaks the war-magic apart with Wren translating the First Tongue's final words, while Sera holds the door against her former colleagues. The bond dies screaming; the beasts go silent. The beat is sacrifice, grief, and terrible relief.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She files a report declaring the wolf-bond extinguished and the child dead—a lie that costs her everything but buys them their lives. Rafael and Wren slip out of the city on Odile's last run. The beat is justice outside the law: imperfect, personal, and quietly paid for.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, with Rafael beside her. The bond is gone, but the beasts still nod to them on the road, and Wren still dreams in the First Tongue—the language outlived its magic. They walk toward no destination in particular, visible at last. The beat is hard-won peace: not safe, not hidden, and finally not alone.
